items.title: UNM's struggles reopen quarterback conversation ahead of pivotal game against Wyoming
items.summary:
The question of who's taking snaps under center is resurfacing in New Mexico football, again.

The question weighs more heavily than usual, thanks to last week's fourth-quarter debacle that resulted in a 21-17 loss to UNLV and ended UNM's small, but hopeful College Football Playoff chances.

items.title: Football: Cracks in offense finally shatter
items.summary:
Saturday's game started strong for the Lobos: wide receiver Bailen George threw a trick-play pass to fellow freshman wide receiver DJ Darling for a 65-yard gain on their second drive of the game, which eventually led to UNM's first touchdown of the night. All was going well.

Fast forward 10 offensive drives, and quarterback Toa Fa'avae and the Lobos' offense had managed only 40 total yards through the air, along with one touchdown pass and an interception.

New Mexico's weakness finally cost them.

items.title: Football: Lobos look to keep up Mountain West dominance against UNLV
items.summary:
The New Mexico Lobos return to Albuquerque on Saturday to play their first game at University Stadium in three weeks, and their first ever on home turf as a nationally-ranked team on the AP Top 25.

The No. 23 Lobos are coming off of a strong 31-3 win at Nevada, hoping to extend their win streak at home to 12. This would tie UNM's all-time record for straight home wins, which began nearly 100 years ago in 1926 and ended in 1928.

items.title: Football: Lobos howl louder
items.summary:
Just when you think Head Coach Jason Eck and his squad can't impress any more, they do.

For the first time in program history, the New Mexico Lobos have won a game in Reno, Nev. The then No. 22-ranked Lobos went on the road and made it look easy out there against the Wolf Pack on Friday night, delivering a 31-3 beatdown.
